page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with Latin, Arabic and italic passages. Running head "NOTÆ." and page number 217 at the top. Two marginal notes in the right margin: "*Seu accessoria essentia." and "lin. 23.". Gathering signature "Ff 2" at the foot.

main_text.p: sentiam suam, ad hanc diflexit, scil. scire Deum per scientiam, & scientiam ejus esse essentiam ejus, Potentem esse per potentiam, & potentiam ejus essentiam ejus esse, vivere per vitam quæ ipsa sit ejus essentia.quam sententiam(inquit) اقتبس من الفلاسفة الذين اعتقدوا ان ذاته واحدة لا كثرة فيها بوجه وانما الصفات ليست وراء الذات معان قايمة بذاته بل ذاته هي desumpsit à Philosophis qui affirmant essentiam Dei unam esse in qua nulla sit omnino multiplicitas, attributa autem [seu proprietates] non esse significata *Seu accessoria essentia.{*}post essentiam subsistentia in essentia ejus, sed ea ipsam esse essentiam. Interim parum abesse visum est Sharestanio, quin Abu Hodail, in eam ob quam Christianos exagitant, & quam tantopere abhorrent AlMotaZali in Deitate, distinctionem inciderit. Si scil. statuat هذه الصفات وجوها للذات essentiæ.

Hoc unanimiter statuunt, Verbum Dei creatum esse, in loco] lin. 23. scil. in subjecto, illud enim est apud Logicos محل. Sic & Sharestanius, de communibus omnium AlMotaZalorum placitis, verba faciens, علي ان كلامه محدث مخلوق في محل وهو حرف وصوت كتب امثا له في المصاحف حكايات عنة فان ما وجد في المحل عرض قن فني في الحال Et in hoc consentiunt quòd sit verbum Dei de novo & creatum in subjecto, ac literis & voce consistere, cujus exemplar in libris scriptum sit, ad ejus imitationem [seu ipsum exprimendum] & quod in subjecto existit, accidens esse & in tempore perire. Idem ex Abu Hodaili sententia, ait, verbum Dei esse بعضه لا في محل وهو قوله

page.notes: Arabic lines are transcribed from a small, low-contrast scan; individual Arabic words are uncertain and should be checked against the original, especially the vowel-less forms in the lines beginning "الذين", "هذه الصفات" and the three lines of Sharestanius' quotation. The asterisk in the text ("* post") is read as a reference mark and transcribed as {*}. The "lin. 23." note is placed beside the start of the "Hoc unanimiter" line. The bracket in "in loco]" is printed as shown. The Latin "defumpsit" is read as "desumpsit", since long s is printed as plain s. The left margin is empty. Show-through and the digitiser's watermark at the bottom right are omitted.
